# CONTRUST

<!-- ## Trust, contestation, and democratic governance -->

CONTRUST is an ERC-funded (2027-2032) project examining whether, when, and how political trust shapes public support for major policy action. The project focuses on climate and the environment, redistribution and inequality, and crime prevention across European democracies.

[Project Overview](project.qmd){.hero-button}

## Overview

::: {.feature-grid}
::: {.feature}
### Research Questions

Political trust is often treated as a vital democratic resource, but we still know too little about its consequences. CONTRUST asks whether trust actually changes support for demanding policies, and under what conditions it does so.
:::

::: {.feature}
### Approach

Over the course of the five years, the project will develop new theory and measures, testing it through a range of methods embedded in an original three-wave panel survey in six countries, on harmonised panel data, and through collaborative meta-studies.
:::

::: {.feature}
### Contribution

CONTRUST develops a new framework for understanding trust as a relationship between citizens, political actors and institutions, and specific policy tasks. It will produce new evidence, open resources, and collaborative analyses for the wider research community.
:::
